sources.entry: (any): build-your-own-x-vibe-coding: BYOX-style tutorials adapted for vibe coding

summary.one_liner: A README-only collection that adapts "build your own X" from-scratch tutorials to an AI-assisted "vibe coding" workflow, with a few tutorial stubs and a long list of planned community showcases.
summary.what_it_does: The repo describes a build style built around short iterative loops (15–25 minutes), reusable prompt recipes for planning, refactors, and tests, minimal runnable scaffolds, and an auto-check at the end of each step. It asks contributors to keep a per-project vibes.md build diary logging intent, friction, and next steps. The README lists AI coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini Cli, Cline, Codex, Cursor) and has a tutorials section with three entries: a Mini-GPT from-scratch LLM in Python, and two video-based entries for building an app and a game in JavaScript/React. Most of the README is a checklist of planned showcase topics (compilers, shells, databases, browsers, and so on), each unchecked. The repo also describes a submission process and a Vibe Loop cheat-sheet. No code, recipes/, checks/, or scaffolds/ directories are referenced as existing in this README.
use_cases: Learn to build a small LLM from scratch with an AI assistant
Find prompt recipes for planning and refactoring side projects
Follow a short build loop for from-scratch projects
Browse planned BYO-X topics to contribute a vibe-coded version
Track a build diary alongside code in vibes.md
stack: AI coding tools named: Claude Code, Gemini Cli, Cline, Codex, Cursor
notable: Frames from-scratch projects around LLM-assisted workflows rather than manual coding
Defines a 15–25 minute micro-loop with an auto-runnable check at each step
Includes a checklist of about 24 BYO-X topics open for community showcases
Credits and extends the codecrafters build-your-own-x list under CC0 1.0
caveats: Most tutorial and showcase entries are placeholders or unchecked items; only a few tutorials are listed
The README references recipes/, checks/, and scaffolds/ folders for contributions, but the README itself does not provide their contents
Not affiliated with CodeCrafters according to the README
